al `expectedSponsored` is how many conversations you expect MCPJam to sponsor; a different actual split is a `409` (`details.code:
swarm_funding_changed`) and nothing is created. The response can report `funding` (`sponsored`, `credits`, `total`) |\n| `GET ...
/goal-runs/{runId}` | The full run: counts, per-target breakdown, per-session `attempts` |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/sessions`
| The chat sessions the run produced (summaries, not transcripts) |\n| `POST .../goal-runs/{runId}/cancel` | Stop a run. Idempote
nt; a second cancel is `200` with `alreadyCanceled: true`, not a `409` |\n\nThree things worth knowing before you write the client

:

* **Always send `Idempotency-Key` on a launch.** It spends model credits, so a
 retry of a dropped response must not run th
e goal twice. Replaying a key\n returns the original run with `deduped: true` and starts no second runner\n and consumes no quot
a. Omitting the header is read as a request that declined\n to identify itself, and gets a fresh run every time.\n* **Check `canc
eled` before reporting a failure.** A stopped run carries\n `status: \"failed\"`, because cancellation is recorded as a marker ra

ther than
 a status of its own. `stale: true` is the third case: the runner went silent
 and the watchdog settled the run.
*
**`targetId`, not `hostId`, identifies a target.** Two environments can\n resolve to the same host with different servers, so a r

un can hold two
 targets that share a `hostId`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Launching **spends**: a run fans out into `targets × itera
tions`\n> sessions. Two different `429`s can come back; the per-minute burst brake\n> (retry in seconds) and your plan's daily lau

nch cap (resets at UTC midnight).
> Both normally carry `Retry-After`; back off on your own when one does not.

**Swarms, insig
hts**: what a run revealed. Read these in order of cost: the\nroll-up and the scorecard are deterministic and free, the findings r

egistry
aggregates them, and swarm run insights run a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goals-overview
` | Project roll-up: recent runs, goal-completion rates, repeat failures, trend |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/scorecard` | One r
un's deterministic rubric result. No model, no spend |\n| `GET .../goal-findings` | Criteria that keep failing, tracked across swa
rm runs |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Hide a finding |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | U
n-hide it |\n| `GET .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Poll a swarm run's generated insights. **404 = nobody asked** |\n| `PO
ST .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Request them. `202`; scheduled, not done |\n| `DELETE .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insig

hts` | Cancel a generation still `pending` |

Two arithmetic traps worth naming, because both produce numbers that look
plausib

le and are wrong:

* **Divide by `sessionsGraded`, never by the session total.** Three failures
 out of four graded sessions,

in a run that attempted forty, is 75%, not
 7.5%.
* **`failedGradingCount` is not `failCount`.** A crashed judge is not a
 re
gression, and folding the two together makes one look like the other.\n\nAnd one modelling note: a finding's `status` is a lifecyc
le:\n`new | recurring | regressed | resolved`. `dismissed` is *not* one of them.\nDismissal is the orthogonal `dismissedAt`, so a

finding can be both recurring
and dismissed, and hiding one never claims it stopped happening.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting s
warm run insights consumes **no credits**; the model cost is on\n> MCPJam. It still counts against the `insightsPerDay` ledger, wh
ich counts\n> REQUESTS and is **shared** with eval-run and user-testing insights, so a\n> request here takes one from there too. P

oll the `GET` rather than
> re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a second slice.
>
> Three refusals, three different
meanings: a short `429` is the per-minute\n> brake (wait seconds), a `429` naming `insightsPerDay` is the daily ledger\n> (its `R
etry-After`, when present, counts to UTC midnight), and a `403` means\n> the feature is not available to your organization; waitin

g will never help.

**User testing** (`/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/study`,
`.../studies/...`): publishin
g an environment for real visitors, reading what\nthey did, and controlling who can reach it. A **study** is a published\nenvironm

ent: one per environment, addressed by its own id once it exists.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `PUT .../environmen
ts/{environmentId}/study` | **Publish.** Idempotent: republishing returns the existing study, and `created: false` says so. Projec
t **admin** |\n| `DELETE .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Unpublish.** The link dies and live sessions end. `deleted: f
alse` when there was nothing published |\n| `PATCH .../studies/{studyId}` | Rename, re-describe, or change `mode` |\n| `GET .../st
udies/{studyId}/sessions` | What visitors did: one row per session, with feedback and a first-message preview |\n| `GET .../studie
s/{studyId}/sessions/{sessionId}` | One session's transcript, paged. Tool payloads and blobs are dropped |\n| `PUT .../studies/{st
udyId}/guest-execution` | The spend dial for anonymous visitors: daily credits, computer starts, concurrency |\n| `POST .../studie
s/{studyId}/rotate-link` | **Mint a new share link.** No body; the new secret is minted server-side |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId
}/members` | Invite someone (or change their role) on an `invited_only` study |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/members/{memberId
OrEmail}` | Remove someone. Their grant is revoked, ending their live sessions |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rebind` | Point th

e study at a different environment in the same project |

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Rotating the link does not evict anyone who alrea
dy used it.** It stops the\n> old URL from granting NEW access; the grants already redeemed under it stay\n> valid. That is the si
ngle most important thing to know here, because rotation\n> is what you reach for when a link leaks, and on its own it does not un

do the
> leak. Rotate *and* remove the members you did not intend to have.
>
> What DOES take effect at once, ending live sessi
ons rather than waiting for\n> expiry: unpublishing, tightening `mode`, and removing a member. Those bump\n> the study's `accessVe
rsion`, and a session minted under an older version\n> stops working. None of them reverse by calling the opposite; a re-invited\n

> member gets a new session, not their old one.
>
> Read `accessVersion` off the publish and rebind responses. The update and
>

rotate responses do not carry it.

**User testing, what visitors did**: the analytics reads, and the model pass
over them. Rea

d these in cost order: metrics, usage and signals are
deterministic and free; the insights request runs a model.

| Endpoint |
What it does |\n| - | - |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/metrics` | Volumes, completion and feedback rates. `?population=real\\|syn
thetic` splits real visitors from swarm runs |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/usage` | Which models, tools and servers the sessions
used. **Check `scan.truncated`** before quoting a rate |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/signals` | What the miner found in the cur
rent window, and where you get the `windowId` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/findings` | Every finding raised over this study, di
smissed ones included |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/windows/{windowId}/insights` | One window's insights. **`404` means nobody a
sked**, which is not the same as `pending` |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | **No credits; counts against `insightsPerD
ay`.** `202` with the `windowId` to poll. `409` if the window has not been mined yet |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/insights`
| Release a generation stuck `pending`. Takes `windowId` in the body |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/dismiss
` | Dismiss a finding. Keyed on its stable id, so it stays dismissed when insights regenerate |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/fin

dings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Undo that |

The `usage` response includes an `analysis` summary: `total`, `analyzed`,
`pending`
, `running`, `failed`, `skipped`, and `deferred` describe session\ncoverage. Failure/skip reasons and `deferredUntil` explain inco
mplete work;\n`awaitingTaxonomy`, `unassigned`, and `staleAssignments` distinguish catalog\ncoverage from extraction. `projectionP
